title_en: Zhu Hongwei’s Application for State Compensation for Wrongful Arrest
ruling_gist_en: The amended State Compensation Law abolished the pre-confirmation procedure for compensation claims. Where a compensation claimant believes that the organ liable for compensation has infringed upon his or her personal or property rights, he or she may directly file a state compensation claim. According to Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the People's Courts' Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, where the Compensation Committee of a People's Court revises a compensation decision that has not yet taken effect made by the organ liable for compensation, the compensation for infringement of personal freedom shall be calculated based on the standard of the national average daily wage of employees in the previous year at the time when the Compensation Committee of the People's Court rendered the compensation decision. Article 35 of the State Compensation Law clarifies compensation for mental damage. The amount of mental distress damages may be determined based on specific circumstances such as the means, occasion, and manner of the infringement, combined with the impact of the infringing act, the negotiation and coordination situation, and the local average living standard.

full_text_en:
Zhu Hongwei v. People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province — State Compensation for Unlawful Arrest

[Ruling Summary]

The amended State Compensation Law abolishes the pre-procedure of compensation confirmation. A compensation claimant who believes that the compensatory obligor has infringed upon his or her personal or property rights may directly file a claim for state compensation. In accordance with Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China by People's Courts, when the Compensation Committee of a People's Court modifies a compensation decision that has not yet become effective and that was made by the compensatory obligor, the compensation for infringement of personal freedom shall be calculated based on the national average daily wage of workers for the year preceding the year in which the Compensation Committee of the People's Court renders the compensation decision. Article 35 of the State Compensation Law specifies compensation for moral damages. The amount of moral damages may be determined based on specific circumstances such as the means, occasion, and manner of the infringement, taking into account the impact of the infringing act, the consultation and coordination situation, and the local average living standard.

Decision on State Compensation by the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 4

Compensation Claimant: Zhu Hongwei, male, born June 25, 1960, Han ethnicity, Chairman of Shenzhen Yihe Industrial Co., Ltd., residing at Room 302, Building 15, North Shekou Zhaoshang Road, Nanshan District, Shenzhen City, Guangdong Province.

Agent ad litem: Li Shuanghui, lawyer, Guangdong Chenggong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Longsheng, paralegal, Guangdong Chenggong Law Firm.

Compensatory Obligor: People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province. Address: No. 1 Huaqiang Road, Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Zheng Hong, Chief Procurator of this Procuratorate.

Agent ad litem: Shen Bingyou, Director of the State Compensation Work Office of this Procuratorate.

Review Organ: Supreme People's Procuratorate of the People's Republic of China. Address: No. 147 Beiheyan Avenue, Dongcheng District, Beijing City.

Legal Representative: Cao Jianming, Chief Procurator of this Procuratorate.

In the case of compensation claimant Zhu Hongwei applying for state compensation for unlawful arrest, dissatisfied with the criminal compensation decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1) made by the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province on July 19, 2011, he applied to the Supreme People's Procuratorate for review. The Supreme People's Procuratorate failed to make a review decision within the time limit. Zhu Hongwei then applied to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision. The Compensation Committee of this Court has lawfully tried this case and now concludes the trial.

Zhu Hongwei alleges: He served as Chairman and Legal Representative of Shenzhen Yihe Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shenzhen Yihe Company) and also operated Wuxi Yihe Electromechanical Co., Ltd. Before his detention, he had substantial income and high social status and reputation. The erroneous detention by the procuratorial organ resulted in the scrapping of his impounded BMW car, the wrongful auction of his personal real estate and the company's factory buildings by the court, overdue payments on his bank credit cards, loss of social insurance and patent rights, the inability of the company to go public, uncollected project accounts, and the freezing of his company shares. His elderly mother suffered severe injuries from a fall due to lack of care, and his then-18-year-old daughter developed depression which remains uncured. He suffered enormous material and moral damages. However, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province only decided to compensate for infringement of personal freedom and did not support other compensation requests. Therefore, he applies to the Compensation Committee of this Court for a compensation decision: 1. Uphold the decision of the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province to pay compensation of RMB 124,254.09 for infringement of personal freedom for 873 days; 2. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province shall apologize, eliminate the impact, and restore reputation through newspaper publications in Shenzhen and Wuxi, and pay RMB 2,000,000 as moral damages; 3. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province shall compensate for the loss of the impounded vehicle, the loss from the auctioned real estate, loss of salary, principal and interest on bank credit card debts, social insurance premiums, loss from the company's inability to go public, and loss of accounts receivable for projects, totaling RMB 29,310,770; 4. Lift the equity freeze on Shenzhen Yihe Company, restore patent rights, exempt taxes for four years, extend the special product license period by four years, and terminate the investment relationship with the criminal case whistleblower Wan Chunhong.

The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province argues: Zhu Hongwei was wrongfully detained for 873 days. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province lawfully decided to pay compensation of RMB 124,254.09 for infringement of personal freedom, has personally apologized to Zhu Hongwei, and has visited relevant industrial and commercial administrative departments and issued explanations to relevant banks to assist Zhu Hongwei in resuming operations. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province did not participate in the impoundment of the vehicle involved and should not bear compensation liability for this. Zhu Hongwei failed to provide evidence of serious consequences of moral damages, and his request for payment of moral damages should not be supported. Other requests do not fall within the scope of state compensation. The criminal compensation decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1) made by the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province was not improper and should be upheld.

Upon trial, the Compensation Committee of this Court finds: On July 25, 2005, the Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau criminally detained Zhu Hongwei on suspicion of contract fraud. On August 24 of the same year, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Procuratorate decided not to approve arrest. On August 26 of the same month, Zhu Hongwei was released on bail pending trial. On May 26, 2006, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province approved the arrest of Zhu Hongwei by Review Decision (Yue Jian Zhen Jian He [2006] No. 4). On June 1 of the same year, Zhu Hongwei was arrested. On February 13, 2007, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Procuratorate filed a public prosecution with the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court by Indictment (Shen Jian Gong Er Xing Su [2007] No. 31), charging Zhu Hongwei with contract fraud. On September 11, 2008, the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court rendered Criminal Judgment ((2007) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 74) finding Zhu Hongwei not guilty due to insufficient evidence. On September 19 of the same month, Zhu Hongwei was released. On September 25 of the same month, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Procuratorate filed a criminal appeal (Shen Jian Gong Er Xing Kang [2008] No. 16) with the Guangdong High People's Court. During the proceedings, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province deemed the appeal improper and withdrew it from the Guangdong High People's Court. On March 25, 2010, the Guangdong High People's Court rendered Criminal Ruling ((2008) Yue Gao Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 326), permitting the withdrawal of the appeal by the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province. Zhu Hongwei was detained for a total of 875 days.

On March 15, 2011, Zhu Hongwei applied to the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province for state compensation on the grounds of wrongful arrest, requesting compensation of RMB 109,500 for infringement of personal freedom for 873 days, RMB 2,000,000 in moral damages, and RMB 29,334,770 in other losses. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province considered that Zhu Hongwei's requests for apology, elimination of impact, restoration of reputation, payment of compensation for infringement of personal freedom, and moral damages should be accepted; other requests did not fall within the scope of compensation of this Procuratorate and were not accepted. On July 19 of the same year, it issued the criminal compensation decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1): 1. Pay compensation for infringement of personal freedom of RMB 124,254.09 (RMB 142.33 x 873 days) based on the national average daily wage of workers for 2010; 2. Verbally apologize and provide convenience within its functional scope to assist Zhu Hongwei in resuming production; 3. Deny the request for payment of moral damages. Zhu Hongwei disagreed and mailed a review application to the Supreme People's Procuratorate on August 2, 2011. The Supreme People's Procuratorate failed to make a review decision within the time limit.

Also found: 1. Zhu Hongwei's daughter Zhu Yizhou was born on July 29, 1987, and was under 18 years old at the time of Zhu Hongwei's criminal detention. Medical records from Suzhou Guangji Hospital and disease certificates from Wuxi Mental Health Center provided by Zhu Hongwei indicate that Zhu Yizhou developed irritable bowel syndrome in 2001, and her depression remained uncured as of February 21, 2012. 2. Since April 4, 2004, Zhu Hongwei served as Chairman and Legal Representative of Shenzhen Yihe Company. The company had not undergone annual inspection since 2005, and its business term expired in 2009 without applying for an extension. However, due to litigation involving its shareholders and frozen equity, its business license had not yet been revoked. 3. Regarding the loss of the impounded vehicle, Zhu Hongwei separately applied to the Shenzhen Municipal Public Security Bureau for compensation. The Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court dismissed Zhu Hongwei's compensation application on the grounds that Zhu Hongwei failed to prove he was the vehicle owner and suffered actual loss. 4. On September 5, 2011, the Guangdong High People's Court, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province, and the Guangdong Provincial Public Security Department jointly issued Yue Gao Fa [2011] No. 382, the Summary of the Symposium on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Moral Damages in State Compensation Work. After the issuance of this summary, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province indicated that moral damages could be paid in accordance with it.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including: Detention Warrant (Shen Gong Jing Zi [2005] No. 082), Review Decision (Yue Jian Zhen Jian He [2006] No. 4), Arrest Warrant (Shen Gong Jing Dai Zi [2006] No. 061), Opinion on Prosecution (Shen Gong Yu Su Zi [2006] No. 211), Indictment (Shen Jian Gong Er Xing Su [2007] No. 31), Criminal Judgment ((2007) Shen Zhong Fa Xing Er Chu Zi No. 74), Release Certificate (Shen Gong Shi Zi [2008] No. 2008073), Criminal Appeal (Shen Jian Gong Er Xing Kang [2008] No. 16), Criminal Ruling ((2008) Yue Gao Fa Xing Er Zhong Zi No. 326), Criminal Compensation Decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1), Postal Express Inquiry Form, Identity Certificate of Zhu Yizhou, Medical Records and Disease Certificates from Suzhou Guangji Hospital et al., Reply Letter (Shen Shi Jian Qi Han [2012] No. 6), Industrial and Commercial Archives of Shenzhen Yihe Company, Decision ((2011) Yue Gao Fa Wei Pei Zi No. 8), and Summary of Symposium (Yue Gao Fa [2011] No. 382).

The Compensation Committee of this Court holds: Compensation claimant Zhu Hongwei submitted his compensation request to the compensatory obligor, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province, on March 15, 2011. This case shall apply the amended State Compensation Law.

Regarding the decision of the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province to pay Zhu Hongwei compensation of RMB 124,254.09 for infringement of personal freedom. Zhu Hongwei was actually detained for 875 days. The calculation of 873 days by the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province was erroneous and should be corrected. In accordance with Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China by People's Courts, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province used the national average daily wage of workers for the year preceding the year of the criminal compensation decision, i.e., 2010, at RMB 142.33 as the compensation standard, which was not improper. However, as the Compensation Committee of this Court modifies a compensation decision of the compensatory obligor that has not yet become effective, the standard should be the national average daily wage of workers for the year preceding the year of this compensation decision, i.e., 2011, at RMB 162.65. Therefore, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province shall pay Zhu Hongwei compensation for infringement of personal freedom for 875 days, totaling RMB 142,318.75, based on the national average daily wage of workers for 2011.

Regarding Zhu Hongwei's request that the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province apologize, eliminate the impact, and restore reputation through newspaper publications in Shenzhen and Wuxi, and pay RMB 2,000,000 in moral damages. Zhu Hongwei was declared not guilty by the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province has already decided to verbally apologize to Zhu Hongwei and provide convenience for the resumption of his production, thereby eliminating the impact and restoring his reputation within the scope of the infringement. This decision should be upheld. Zhu Hongwei's additional request for the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province to apologize through newspaper publications is not supported. Zhu Hongwei was detained for 875 days, and his normal family life and company operations were affected as a result. It should be determined that the consequences of moral damages were serious. After the issuance of Yue Gao Fa [2011] No. 382, the Summary of the Symposium on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Moral Damages in State Compensation Work, the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province indicated that moral damages could be paid in accordance with this summary. For the moral damages claimed by Zhu Hongwei, the Compensation Committee of this Court determines the amount as RMB 50,000 based on the actual circumstances of this case.

Zhu Hongwei's application for the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province to compensate for the loss of the impounded vehicle is rejected because the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province did not impound the vehicle, and the Compensation Committee of the Guangdong High People's Court found in a separate case that Zhu Hongwei was not the vehicle owner, making his application legally unfounded. Zhu Hongwei's request for compensation for the loss from the auctioned real estate is unrelated to the official acts of the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province and is not supported. Zhu Hongwei's other requests, including compensation for loss of salary, principal and interest on bank credit card debts, social insurance premiums, loss from the company's inability to go public, loss of accounts receivable for projects, lifting the equity freeze on the company, restoring patent rights, exempting taxes, extending the special product license period, and terminating the investment relationship, do not fall within the scope of compensation under the State Compensation Law and are not supported.

In summary, in accordance with Articles 25, Paragraph 3 of Article 29, Article 33, and Article 35 of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China, Item (2) of Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China (I), Articles 19 and 20 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Procedures for the Compensation Committee of People's Courts to Hear State Compensation Cases, and Article 6 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the State Compensation Law of the People's Republic of China by People's Courts, the Compensation Committee of this Court decides as follows:

1. Uphold Item 2 of the Criminal Compensation Decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1) of the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province;

2. Revoke Items 1 and 3 of the Criminal Compensation Decision (Yue Jian Pei Jue [2011] No. 1) of the People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province;

3. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province shall pay Zhu Hongwei compensation for infringement of personal freedom in the amount of RMB 142,318.75;

4. The People's Procuratorate of Guangdong Province shall pay Zhu Hongwei moral damages in the amount of RMB 50,000;

5. Dismiss all other compensation requests of Zhu Hongwei.

This decision is legally effective.

June 18, 2012
